question.text: Find $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 0^{-}}f(x)$ and $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \left(\pi/2\right)^{+}}f(x)$ for the function given by \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} 2\sec x &\textrm{ for }\quad -\dfrac{\pi}{2} < x < 0 \\[5pt] \cot x + x &\textrm{ for }\quad \dfrac{\pi}{2}\leq x < \pi. \end{cases} \]
question.explanation:
Approaching $x=0$ from the left, we have $x\lt 0,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=2\sec x.$ We get

\begin{align} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 0^{-}}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 0^{-}} 2\sec x\\[3pt] &=2\sec 0\\[3pt] &=2(1)\\[3pt] &=2. \end{align}

Approaching $x=\dfrac {\pi}{2}$ from the right, we have $x \gt \dfrac{\pi}{2},$ so we use the expression $f(x)=\cot x +x.$ We get

\begin{align} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \left(\pi/2\right)^{+}}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \left(\pi/2\right)^{+}} \left(\cot x +x\right)\\[3pt] &=\cot \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\\[3pt] &=0+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\\[3pt] &=\dfrac{\pi}{2}. \end{align}

example.title: Computing Limits of Piecewise Functions with a Gap in the Domain

question.text: For the piecewise function \[ f(x) = \begin{cases} x^2+x-1 \quad &\textrm{ for }\quad x< 2\\ x^2+bx+3 \quad &\textrm{ for }\quad x>2 \end{cases} \] it is known that $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2}f(x)$ exists. What is the value of the constant $b?$
question.explanation:
In order for $\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2}f(x)$ to exist, the left and right-sided limits must both exist and be equal.

  • Approaching from the left, we have $x < 2,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=x^2+x-1.$ We get \begin{align} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2^{-}}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2^{-}} x^2+x-1 \\[3pt] &= (2)^2 + 2 -1 \\[3pt] &=5. \end{align}

  • Approaching from the right, we have $x>2,$ so we use the expression $f(x)= x^2+bx+3.$ We get \begin{align} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2^{+}}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2^{+}} x^2+bx+3 \\[3pt] &= (2)^2 + b\cdot 2 + 3\\[3pt] &=7+2b. \end{align}

Finally, since the left and right-sided limits must be equal, we have \begin{align} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2^{-}}f(x) &= \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2^{+}}f(x) \\[3pt] 5 &= 7 + 2b \\[3pt] 2b &= -2\\[3pt] b &= -1. \end{align}

example.title: Solving for a Constant Such that the Limit of a Piecewise Function Exists

question.text:
Find the right-sided limit at $x=2$ for the function
\[
f(x) = 
\begin{cases}
x^4 - 16 \quad    &\textrm{ for }\quad x\leq 2 \\[5pt]
\sqrt{2x+5} - \sqrt{2x}  \quad   &\textrm{ for }\quad x > 2.
\end{cases}
\]
question.explanation: Approaching from the right, we have $x>2,$ so we use the expression $f(x)=\sqrt{2x+5} - \sqrt{2x}.$ We get \begin{align} \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2^{+}}f(x)&=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2^{+}} \left(\sqrt{2x+5} - \sqrt{2x}\right) \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{(2\cdot 2) + 5} - \sqrt{2\cdot 2} \\[3pt] &= \sqrt{9} - \sqrt{4} \\[3pt] &= 3 - 2 \\[3pt] &= \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{1}. \end{align}
